HEEWON STYLE — a KOREAN WEBTOON movie still PAINTED like a premium digital painting, the look of a dramatic manhwa cover. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). The shot the scene names (wide establishing, two-shot, close-up, over-the-shoulder) from a dramatic camera angle (low three-quarter, worm's-eye, high overhead or dutch), never a flat straight-on catalogue pose. Named characters' FACES are drawn exactly like the attached character sheet: the same confident ink linework drawn BOLD and THICK with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands and manhwa face design (eye shape, brows, nose, jaw, hairline and hair), recognisably those characters, in the clothes the scene gives them. EVERYTHING ELSE IS PAINTED: visible textured brushwork — loose digital-paint strokes and dry-brush, charcoal-like hatching that follow every fold of the silk and every plate of armour, the shadows built from layered strokes, the brightest ridges laid in with single confident strokes, a faint paper-and-canvas grain; at the edges of the garments the linework breaks into loose sketchy strokes. NOT flat cel-shading, NOT smooth airbrushed gradients, NOT a clean vector look, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D. Wide-medium shot, low angle from water level, steam cavern at night. Centre: Munmu, unclothed, wet hair loose, chest-deep in black water, looking from side to side, overwhelmed. LEFT, standing on the water: Park Hyukgose, a radiantly beautiful young king in white and pale-blue silk with a gold crown, a farmer's calm, and beside him Lady Alyoung in pale ice-blue silk with her jade hairpin, sharp-eyed. RIGHT, standing on the water: King Suro in purple silk with a small gold crown, grinning, and beside him Queen Heo in close-fitted rose-pink silk with her gold hairpin, composed and amused. ONE device: the two couples as two pillars framing the king, mirrored in the still water. The four founders are numinous demigods painted photoreal-leaning, real skin; Munmu is painterly webtoon. Steam drifts at their hems; one pale shaft from above. Pale blue #6f9fe8 catch on the left, amber-gold #e0a33c catch on the right. Each of the five is a different person; do not clone faces. Munmu in the spring: take ONLY his FACE from the sheet — no crown, no robe, no cap, no headband; bare-headed, wet hair loose, unclothed, nothing on but water. REFERENCE SHEET. TOP ROW, left to right: LEFT face = munmu, SECOND face = hyukgose, THIRD face = alyoung, FOURTH face = suro, FIFTH face = heohwangok. Copy each face exactly; give each person the dress the scene names. SMALLER SECOND ROW, left to right: costume chart (cut and shape only; ignore its labels, poses and faces), binyeo board alyoung (her hair ornament exactly; not clothing), binyeo board heo (her hair ornament exactly; not clothing), crown reference (shape only). KING MUNMU — Look: Square jaw, goatee and moustache, confident grin; arms folded when he is pleased with himself. Dress: As king: crimson robe with gold dragon embroidery, blue shoulder pieces, gold Silla crown. Earlier: prince/hwarang stage portraits. Crown: Silla gold crown, copied from the attached Cheonmachong museum photo: a broad sheet-gold band with three tall tree-shaped uprights stepped like the character 出 (three tiers of short arms turned up into heart-shaped tips) and two antler uprights at the sides, hung with hundreds of round gold spangles on wires and many curved pale-green jade gogok, two long chains of gold leaf pendants falling from the temples to the collarbones. Thin bright sheet gold, never a European spiked crown, never a solid cast crown or a tiara. Colour #C41E3A. HYUKGOSÉ — Crown: Silla gold crown, copied from the attached Cheonmachong museum photo: a broad sheet-gold band with three tall tree-shaped uprights stepped like the character 出 (three tiers of short arms turned up into heart-shaped tips) and two antler uprights at the sides, hung with hundreds of round gold spangles on wires and many curved pale-green jade gogok, two long chains of gold leaf pendants falling from the temples to the collarbones. Thin bright sheet gold, never a European spiked crown, never a solid cast crown or a tiara. Colour #6f9fe8. LADY ALYOUNG — Crown: Silla gold crown, copied from the attached Cheonmachong museum photo: a broad sheet-gold band with three tall tree-shaped uprights stepped like the character 出 (three tiers of short arms turned up into heart-shaped tips) and two antler uprights at the sides, hung with hundreds of round gold spangles on wires and many curved pale-green jade gogok, two long chains of gold leaf pendants falling from the temples to the collarbones. Thin bright sheet gold, never a European spiked crown, never a solid cast crown or a tiara. Colour #a8c8f0. KING SURO — Look: His portrait face: young, warm, a thin moustache and goatee, black hair under a little gold crown. Dress: Purple silk robe with gold-ochre collar bands and sash, as on his portrait. Crown: Gaya gold crown: a gold band with tall upright grass-leaf finials and hanging jade gogok. Now: As a ghost in the steam cavern (647) he keeps his portrait's young face, purple silk and little gold crown — never an old white-bearded hermit; barefoot, feet in the water, delighted with himself. Colour #e0a33c. QUEEN HU — Look: South Indian princess from Ayuta: deep warm brown skin, clearly darker than every Gaya and Samhan face around her; large dark kohl-lined eyes, full lips, straight nose, blue-black hair coiled low with the purple-tiger binyeo, small gold hoop earrings. Dress: Her portrait silk: violet-purple jeogori with magenta-gold patterned sleeves and cream cuffs, deep violet chima, pale gold sash with tassels. Cut close and tailored: the jacket fitted to the bust and waist, the sash cinched high, the skirt falling clean from the hips; elegant and expensive, never loose, never a sari dump, never pink. Crown: Gaya gold crown: a gold band with tall upright grass-leaf finials and hanging jade gogok. Colour #d98fa8. BACKGROUND AND LIGHT (painterly tenebrism): the background IS the place and the moment of the scene — open sky if they are in the sky, the hall if they are in a hall, the gate, the river, the snow — painted loosely in atmospheric brushwork (drifting smoke, cloud, haze, mist, falling snow, embers) in the scene's own colours, soft and out of focus, with a faint bokeh of small lights; it has colour, weather and depth — never a flat black void, never a detailed set; crowds and armies only as massed painted shapes dissolving into haze. ONE hard directional key light that belongs to the place (a brazier, a lamp, the sun through cloud, a torch, moonlight) rakes across the faces and clothes from the side or from below, modelling them in high contrast with deep painted shadows and a thin edge of the same light along the silhouette. Each character's colour lives in that light and in the atmosphere around them — never a glow aura or halo. Faces and bodies act the beat: real expressions, real weight, mid-motion. Faces from the sheet; new poses, never the sheet's stance. Each named person appears once, never cloned. Everyone wears period clothing of their own court (Korean, Tang, Yamato, Mohe furs), never European dress. No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark. NIGHT GROUND: the frame is built on BLACK — crushed ink-black night masses around the subject, the place pulled out of the dark only where the one key light (fire, lamp, torch, moon) falls, small warm bokeh in the black; the figure is the bright thing in a dark frame.
